title_en: Administrative Compulsion Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of regulating the establishment and implementation of administrative compulsion, ensuring and supervising administrative organs in performing their duties according to law, safeguarding public interests and social order, and protecting the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, administrative compulsion includes administrative compulsory measures and administrative compulsory enforcement.
Administrative compulsory measures mean the acts where administrative organs, in the course of administrative management, temporarily restrict the personal freedom of citizens or temporarily control the property of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations according to law for the purposes of stopping illegal acts, preventing destruction of evidence, avoiding occurrence of harm, or controlling expansion of danger.
Administrative compulsory enforcement means the acts where administrative organs, or administrative organs applying to a People's Court, take compulsory measures according to law to compel the performance of obligations by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations that fail to perform the obligations determined in administrative decisions.

Article 3 The establishment and implementation of administrative compulsion shall be governed by this Law.
Where an emergency such as a natural disaster, accident disaster, public health incident, or social security incident occurs or is imminent, and administrative organs take emergency measures or provisional measures, such measures shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Where administrative organs take prudential supervision measures in the financial industry or compulsory technical monitoring measures for inbound and outbound goods, such measures shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 4 The establishment and implementation of administrative compulsion shall be in accordance with the statutory authority, scope, conditions, and procedures.

Article 5 The establishment and implementation of administrative compulsion shall be appropriate. Where the objectives of administrative management can be achieved by non-compulsory means, no administrative compulsion shall be established or implemented.
Article 6 In implementing administrative compulsion, the principle of combining education with compulsion shall be adhered to.
Article 7 No administrative organ or its staff member may use the power of administrative compulsion to seek gains for any unit or individual.

Article 8 Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations shall, with respect to the implementation of administrative compulsion by administrative organs, have the right to make statements and to defend themselves; have the right to apply for administrative reconsideration or to bring an administrative action according to law; and if they suffer damage due to the illegal implementation of administrative compulsion by administrative organs, have the right to claim compensation according to law.
Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations that suffer damage due to illegal acts committed by a People's Court in compulsory enforcement or due to the expansion of the scope of compulsory enforcement shall have the right to claim compensation according to law.

Article 10 Administrative compulsory measures shall be established by law.
Where no law has been enacted, and the matter falls within the administrative functions of the State Council, administrative regulations may establish administrative compulsory measures other than those specified in Items (1) and (4) of Article 9 of this Law and those that shall be prescribed by law.
Where no law or administrative regulation has been enacted, and the matter is a local affair, local regulations may establish the administrative compulsory measures specified in Items (2) and (3) of Article 9 of this Law.
No regulatory document other than laws and regulations may establish administrative compulsory measures.

Article 11 Where a law has prescribed the targets, conditions, and types of administrative compulsory measures, administrative regulations and local regulations may not make provisions that expand them.
Where a law has not established any administrative compulsory measure, administrative regulations and local regulations may not establish any administrative compulsory measure. However, where a law provides that specific matters shall be subject to specific management measures prescribed by administrative regulations, the administrative regulations may establish administrative compulsory measures other than those specified in Items (1) and (4) of Article 9 of this Law and those that shall be prescribed by law.

Article 13 Administrative compulsory enforcement shall be established by law.
Where a law does not prescribe compulsory enforcement by an administrative organ, the administrative organ that made the administrative decision shall apply to a People's Court for compulsory enforcement.

Article 14 When drafting a bill of a law or a draft regulation that intends to establish administrative compulsion, the drafting unit shall solicit opinions through forms such as hearings or feasibility study meetings, and shall explain to the enacting organ the necessity of establishing such administrative compulsion, the possible impact thereof, and the opinions solicited and adopted.

Article 15 The organ that establishes administrative compulsion shall periodically evaluate the administrative compulsion it has established, and promptly amend or abolish any inappropriate administrative compulsion.
The organ that implements administrative compulsion may timely evaluate the implementation status and the necessity of existing administrative compulsion, and report its opinions to the organ that established such administrative compulsion.
Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations may raise opinions and suggestions to the organ that establishes administrative compulsion and the organ that implements it regarding the establishment and implementation of administrative compulsion. The relevant organ shall seriously study and demonstrate such opinions and suggestions, and provide feedback in an appropriate manner.

Article 16 Where an administrative organ performs its administrative management duties, it shall impose administrative compulsion measures in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
If the illegal act is of a clearly minor nature or has no evident social harm, administrative compulsion measures may not be taken.

Article 17 Administrative compulsion measures shall be implemented by the administrative organs prescribed by laws and regulations within their statutory functions and powers. The power to impose administrative compulsion measures shall not be delegated.
An administrative organ that exercises relatively centralized administrative penalty powers in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China may implement the administrative compulsion measures related to the administrative penalty powers as prescribed by laws and regulations.
Administrative compulsion measures shall be implemented by qualified administrative law enforcement personnel of the administrative organ; other personnel shall not implement them.

Article 19 In an emergency where an administrative compulsion measure needs to be taken on the spot, the administrative law enforcement personnel shall report to the person in charge of the administrative organ within twenty-four hours and go through the approval procedures retroactively. If the person in charge of the administrative organ considers that the administrative compulsion measure should not have been taken, the measure shall be immediately lifted.

Article 21 Where an illegal act is suspected of constituting a crime and shall be referred to a judicial organ, the administrative organ shall transfer the sealed up, seized, or frozen property together and notify the party in writing.
Article 22 Seizure and impoundment shall be implemented by the administrative organs prescribed by laws and regulations; no other administrative organ or organization shall implement them.

Article 23 Seizure and impoundment shall be limited to the premises, facilities, or property involved in the case; the premises, facilities, or property unrelated to the illegal act shall not be sealed up or seized; the daily necessities of the individual citizen and his dependent family members shall not be sealed up or seized.
Where the premises, facilities, or property of the party have already been sealed up by another state organ according to law, they shall not be sealed up again.

Article 25 The period for seizure and impoundment shall not exceed thirty days; if the circumstances are complex, with the approval of the person in charge of the administrative organ, the period may be extended, but the extended period shall not exceed thirty days, unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.
A decision to extend seizure and impoundment shall be notified in writing to the party in a timely manner, and the reasons shall be explained.
Where an item needs to be tested, inspected, quarantined, or subjected to technical appraisal, the period for seizure and impoundment shall not include the period for testing, inspection, quarantine, or technical appraisal. The period for testing, inspection, quarantine, or technical appraisal shall be clearly defined and notified in writing to the party. The costs of testing, inspection, quarantine, or technical appraisal shall be borne by the administrative organ.

Article 26 With respect to the premises, facilities, or property being sealed up or seized, the administrative organ shall properly keep them and shall not use or damage them; if losses are caused, the administrative organ shall bear compensation liability.
With respect to the premises, facilities, or property being sealed up, the administrative organ may entrust a third party to keep them, and the third party shall not damage or transfer or dispose of them without authorization. Where losses are caused due to the reasons of the third party, the administrative organ, after making compensation first, shall have the right to seek recourse from the third party.
The storage costs incurred due to seizure and impoundment shall be borne by the administrative organ.

Article 27 After taking measures of seizure and impoundment, the administrative organ shall promptly ascertain the facts and make a handling decision within the time limit prescribed in Article 25 of this Law. Where the illegal facts are clear and the illegal property shall be confiscated according to law, it shall be confiscated; where laws and administrative regulations prescribe that it shall be destroyed, it shall be destroyed according to law; where seizure and impoundment shall be lifted, a decision to lift the seizure and impoundment shall be made.

Article 29 Freezing of deposits and remittances shall be implemented by the administrative organs prescribed by law and shall not be delegated to other administrative organs or organizations; no other administrative organ or organization shall freeze deposits or remittances.
The amount of deposits and remittances frozen shall be commensurate with the amount involved in the illegal act; where they have already been frozen by another state organ according to law, they shall not be frozen again.

Article 30 Where an administrative organ decides to freeze deposits and remittances in accordance with legal provisions, it shall fulfill the procedures prescribed in items (1), (2), (3), and (7) of Article 18 of this Law, and shall deliver a freeze notice to the financial institution.
Upon receiving the freeze notice lawfully made by the administrative organ, the financial institution shall immediately freeze the deposits and remittances, shall not delay, and shall not disclose information to the party before the freeze.
Where an administrative organ or organization other than those prescribed by law requests to freeze the deposits and remittances of a party, the financial institution shall refuse.

Article 32 Within thirty days from the date of freezing the deposits and remittances, the administrative organ shall make a handling decision or a decision to lift the freeze; if the circumstances are complex, with the approval of the person in charge of the administrative organ, the period may be extended, but the extended period shall not exceed thirty days, unless otherwise provided by law.
A decision to extend the freeze shall be notified in writing to the party in a timely manner, and the reasons shall be explained.

Article 34 After an administrative organ makes an administrative decision according to law, if the party fails to perform its obligations within the time limit specified in the decision, the administrative organ having the power of administrative compulsory enforcement shall enforce the decision compulsorily in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Article 36 A party shall have the right to make statements and defend itself after receiving the notice of催告. The administrative organ shall fully hear the opinions of the party, and shall record and review the facts, reasons and evidence submitted by the party. If the facts, reasons or evidence submitted by the party are established, the administrative organ shall adopt them.

Article 38 The notice of催告 and the written decision on compulsory enforcement shall be served directly on the party. If the party refuses to accept the service or if direct service is impossible, the service shall be effected in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 41 If, during or after enforcement, the administrative decision on which the enforcement is based is revoked or changed, or if the enforcement is erroneous, the original state shall be restored or the property shall be returned; if restoration of the original state or return of the property is impossible, compensation shall be made according to law.

Article 42 When implementing compulsory enforcement, the administrative organ may, without harming the public interest or the lawful rights and interests of others, reach an enforcement agreement with the party. The enforcement agreement may stipulate performance by installments; if the party takes remedial measures, the additional fine or surcharge may be reduced or waived.
The enforcement agreement shall be performed. If the party fails to perform the enforcement agreement, the administrative organ shall resume compulsory enforcement.

Article 43 An administrative organ shall not implement compulsory enforcement at night or on legal holidays, except in emergency situations.
An administrative organ shall not compel a party to perform a relevant administrative decision by cutting off water, electricity, heat, or gas supply for residents' daily life.

Article 44 If illegal buildings, structures, or facilities need to be forcibly demolished, the administrative organ shall issue a public notice and set a time limit for the party to demolish them voluntarily. If the party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor institutes administrative proceedings within the statutory time limit, nor demolishes them, the administrative organ may forcibly demolish them according to law.

Article 45 If an administrative organ makes an administrative decision on a monetary payment obligation according to law and the party fails to perform it within the time limit, the administrative organ may impose an additional fine or surcharge according to law. The standard for the additional fine or surcharge shall be notified to the party.
The amount of the additional fine or surcharge shall not exceed the amount of the monetary payment obligation.

Article 46 If an administrative organ imposes an additional fine or surcharge for more than thirty days in accordance with Article 45 of this Law, and the party still fails to perform after催告, the administrative organ with the power of compulsory enforcement may enforce compulsorily.
If an administrative organ needs to adopt measures of seizure, impoundment, or freezing before implementing compulsory enforcement, it shall handle the matter in accordance with the provisions of Chapter III of this Law.
An administrative organ without the power of compulsory enforcement shall apply to a People's Court for compulsory enforcement. However, if the party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor institutes administrative proceedings within the statutory time limit, and still fails to perform after催告, the administrative organ that has already taken measures of seizure or impoundment during the process of administrative management may auction the seized or impounded property according to law to offset the fine.

Article 47 The transfer of deposits or remittances shall be decided by the administrative organ prescribed by law, and the financial institution shall be notified in writing. After receiving the decision on transfer of deposits or remittances made by the administrative organ according to law, the financial institution shall immediately execute the transfer.
If an administrative organ or organization other than those prescribed by law requests the transfer of a party's deposits or remittances, the financial institution shall refuse.

Article 48 The auction of property according to law shall be handled by an auction institution entrusted by the administrative organ in accordance with the provisions of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 49 The transferred deposits, remittances, and proceeds from auction and lawful disposal shall be turned over to the State Treasury or transferred to a special fiscal account. No administrative organ or individual may in any form intercept, privately distribute, or covertly distribute them.

Article 50 If an administrative organ makes an administrative decision according to law requiring a party to perform obligations such as removing an obstruction or restoring the original state, and the party fails to perform within the time limit and still fails to perform after催告, and the consequences have endangered or will endanger traffic safety, cause environmental pollution, or damage natural resources, the administrative organ may perform the act vicariously, or entrust a disinterested third party to do so.

Article 52 If spills, obstacles, or contaminants on roads, waterways, channels, or public places need to be immediately cleared, and the party is unable to do so, the administrative organ may decide to implement vicarious performance immediately; if the party is not present, the administrative organ shall notify the party immediately afterward and handle the matter according to law.

Article 53 Where a party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor brings an administrative action within the statutory time limit, nor performs the administrative decision, an administrative organ that does not have the power of administrative compulsory enforcement may, within three months from the date of expiry of the time limit, apply to a People's Court for compulsory enforcement in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Article 54 Before applying to a People's Court for compulsory enforcement, the administrative organ shall urge the party to perform the obligation. If the party still fails to perform the obligation ten days after the service of the reminder letter, the administrative organ may apply to the People's Court that has jurisdiction in the place where it is located for compulsory enforcement; where the subject of enforcement is immovable property, it shall apply to the People's Court that has jurisdiction in the place where the immovable property is located for compulsory enforcement.

Article 56 A People's Court shall accept an application for compulsory enforcement submitted by an administrative organ within five days.
If the administrative organ objects to the People's Court's ruling of non-acceptance, it may, within fifteen days, apply for reconsideration to the next higher People's Court, which shall make a ruling on whether to accept the case within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the application for reconsideration.

Article 57 A People's Court shall conduct a written examination of the administrative organ's application for compulsory enforcement. If the application is in compliance with the provisions of Article 55 of this Law and the administrative decision has statutory enforcement effect, the People's Court shall, except under the circumstances specified in Article 58 of this Law, make an enforcement ruling within seven days from the date of acceptance.

Article 58 Where a People's Court finds any of the following circumstances, it may hear the opinions of the person subject to enforcement and the administrative organ before making a ruling:
(1) the fact is obviously insufficient;
(2) the basis of laws or regulations is obviously lacking; or
(3) other circumstances in which the act is obviously illegal and impairs the lawful rights and interests of the person subject to enforcement.
The People's Court shall, within 30 days from the date of acceptance, make a ruling on whether to enforce. If the ruling is not to enforce, the People's Court shall state the reasons and shall serve the ruling of non-enforcement on the administrative organ within 5 days.
If the administrative object has any objection to the People's Court's ruling of non-enforcement, it may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the ruling, apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration. The People's Court at the next higher level shall, within 30 days from the date of receipt of the application for reconsideration, make a ruling on whether to enforce.

Article 59 In cases of emergency, for the protection of public safety, the administrative organ may apply to the People's Court for immediate enforcement. With the approval of the chief judge of the People's Court, the People's Court shall enforce within 5 days from the date of making the ruling of enforcement.

Article 60 Where an administrative organ applies to the People's Court for compulsory enforcement, it shall not pay an application fee. The costs of compulsory enforcement shall be borne by the person subject to enforcement.
Where the People's Court enforces by means of transfer or auction, it may deduct the costs of compulsory enforcement after the transfer or auction.
Where property is auctioned according to law, the People's Court shall entrust an auction institution to handle the matter in accordance with the provisions of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China.
The transferred deposits, remittances, and the proceeds from auction and lawful disposal shall be turned over to the national treasury or transferred into a special fiscal account, and shall not be withheld, distributed among individuals, or disguisedly distributed among individuals in any form.

Article 63 Where an administrative organ withholds, distributes among individuals, or disguisedly distributes among individuals the sealed-up or seized property, or the transferred deposits, remittances, or the proceeds from auction and lawful disposal, the finance department or the relevant department shall recover the illegal gains; and the persons directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions such as a major demerit, demotion, removal from office, or expulsion according to law.
Where a staff member of an administrative organ, taking advantage of his position, appropriates the sealed-up or seized premises, facilities or property, the administrative organ at the next higher level or the relevant department shall order him to make corrections, and he shall be given sanctions such as a major demerit, demotion, removal from office, or expulsion according to law.

Article 64 Where an administrative organ or its staff member takes advantage of the power of administrative compulsion to seek benefits for a unit or individual, the administrative organ at the next higher level or the relevant department shall order it to make corrections, and the persons directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 66 Where a financial institution, in violation of the provisions of this Law, transfers the funds into an account other than the national treasury or a special fiscal account, the financial regulatory authority shall order it to make corrections and shall impose a fine of two times the amount of the illegally transferred funds; and the persons directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where an administrative organ or a People's Court, in violation of the provisions of this Law, instructs a financial institution to transfer funds into an account other than the national treasury or a special fiscal account, the persons directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 67 Where a People's Court or its staff member commits an illegal act in the compulsory enforcement or expands the scope of compulsory enforcement, the persons directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 68 Any violation of the provisions of this Law that causes losses to a citizen, legal person or other organization shall be compensated according to law.
Any violation of the provisions of this Law that constitutes a crime shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.
Article 69 The provisions in this Law on a period of ten days or less refer to working days, excluding statutory holidays.

Article 70 Where an organization authorized by law or administrative regulations to have the function of managing public affairs implements administrative compulsion in its own name within the scope of statutory authorization, the provisions of this Law on administrative organs shall apply.
Article 71 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2012.
